servers.name: tracehub-mcp
servers.description: 跨 Jaeger、Tempo、Traceloop、Datadog、Sentry、X-Ray、New Relic、Honeycomb 查询 OTel 跟踪。

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_TYPE
requiredEnv.description: Which observability backend to query.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_URL
requiredEnv.description: Backend API endpoint, e.g. http://localhost:16686 for Jaeger, https://api.datadoghq.com for Datadog, https://api.newrelic.com/graphql for New Relic, or https://api.honeycomb.io for Honeycomb. For the X-Ray backend this is decorative only (e.g. https://xray.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) - never dereferenced for a live request.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: API key or auth token. Required for Traceloop, Datadog, Sentry, New Relic, and Honeycomb; not used by Jaeger, Tempo, or X-Ray. For New Relic this must be a User API key, not an Ingest or License key; for Honeycomb this must be a Configuration Key, not an Ingest or Management key.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_AWS_REGION
requiredEnv.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Required for the X-Ray backend only - X-Ray authenticates via boto3's standard AWS credential chain, not BACKEND_API_KEY.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_NEWRELIC_ACCOUNT_ID
requiredEnv.description: New Relic account ID, required for the New Relic backend only - NerdGraph queries are user-scoped, not account-scoped, so this identifies which account's data to read.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_HONEYCOMB_DATASET
requiredEnv.description: Honeycomb dataset slug, required for the Honeycomb backend only - the Query Data API is dataset-scoped.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_APP_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Datadog Application key, required in addition to BACKEND_API_KEY for the Datadog backend only.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_TEMPO_INSTANCE_ID
requiredEnv.description: Grafana Cloud stack/instance ID, used with BACKEND_API_KEY for Basic Auth (Tempo backend only, required for Grafana Cloud-hosted Tempo, not needed for self-hosted Tempo).

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_SENTRY_ORG
requiredEnv.description: Sentry organization slug, required for the Sentry backend only.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_SENTRY_PROJECT
requiredEnv.description: Sentry project slug, optional for the Sentry backend - narrows queries to one project.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_ENVIRONMENTS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated environments for the Traceloop backend only.

requiredEnv.name: BACKEND_TIMEOUT
requiredEnv.description: Request timeout in seconds.

requiredEnv.name: LOG_LEVEL
requiredEnv.description: Logging level.

requiredEnv.name: MAX_TRACES_PER_QUERY
requiredEnv.description: Maximum traces validated per query (1-1000).

requiredEnv.name: SLOW_REQUEST_THRESHOLD_MS
requiredEnv.description: Logs a WARNING for any backend request slower than this, independent of LOG_LEVEL. Unset disables slow-request logging.

requiredEnv.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
requiredEnv.description: Enables opt-in OTel self-instrumentation of tool calls when set. Unset means zero overhead - no TracerProvider is configured and no middleware is registered.

requiredEnv.name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
requiredEnv.description: Service name reported in self-instrumentation spans, only used when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set.

requiredEnv.name: MCP_INCLUDE_ARGS_IN_SPANS
requiredEnv.description: Include tool call arguments/results as OTel span attributes when self-instrumentation is enabled. Off by default since they may contain sensitive data.

requiredEnv.description: When set to true, allows configuration values to be overridden via request headers and query parameters.

requiredEnv.description: Atlas API client ID for authentication. Required for running Atlas tools.

requiredEnv.description: Atlas API client secret for authentication. Required for running Atlas tools.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL
requiredEnv.description: Base URL for the MongoDB Assistant API.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_ATLAS_TEMPORARY_DATABASE_USER_LIFETIME_MS
requiredEnv.description: Time in milliseconds that temporary database users created when connecting to MongoDB Atlas clusters will remain active before being automatically deleted.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_TOOLS
requiredEnv.description: Comma separated values of tool names that require user confirmation before execution. Requires the client to support elicitation.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_SCOPE
requiredEnv.description: Visibility scope for MongoDB connections created at runtime. With 'session' (the default), each MCP session only sees the connections it created (plus the shared 'preconfigured' one) and they are closed when the session ends — recommended when the HTTP transport is exposed to multiple clients without authentication. With 'global', connections are shared across all sessions and survive session rotation.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING
requiredEnv.description: MongoDB connection string for direct database connections. Optional, if not set, you'll need to call the connect tool before interacting with MongoDB data.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_DISABLE_SERVER_SIDE_JS
requiredEnv.description: When set to true, disallows the use of server-side JavaScript operators (such as $where, $function, and $accumulator) in query filters and aggregation pipelines.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS
requiredEnv.description: Comma separated values of tool names, operation types, and/or categories of tools that will be disabled.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_DRY_RUN
requiredEnv.description: When true, runs the server in dry mode: dumps configuration and enabled tools, then exits without starting the server.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_ELICITATION_TIMEOUT_MS
requiredEnv.description: Time in milliseconds the user has to respond to an elicitation request (such as a tool confirmation prompt) before it fails.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_EXPORT_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS
requiredEnv.description: Time in milliseconds between export cleanup cycles that remove expired export files.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_MS
requiredEnv.description: Time in milliseconds after which an export is considered expired and eligible for cleanup.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_EXPORTS_PATH
requiredEnv.description: Folder to store exported data files.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_EXTERNALLY_MANAGED_SESSIONS
requiredEnv.description: When true, the HTTP transport allows requests with a session ID supplied externally through the 'mcp-session-id' header. When an external ID is supplied, the initialization request is optional.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HEALTH_CHECK_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Deprecated. Use `monitoringServerHost` instead. Host address to bind the healthCheck HTTP server to (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `healthCheckPort` must also be set.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HEALTH_CHECK_PORT
requiredEnv.description: Deprecated. Use `monitoringServerPort` instead. Port number for the healthCheck HTTP server (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `healthCheckHost` must also be set.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HTTP_BODY_LIMIT
requiredEnv.description: Maximum size of the HTTP request body in bytes (only used when transport is 'http'). This value is passed as the optional limit parameter to the Express.js json() middleware.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS
requiredEnv.description: Header that the HTTP server will validate when making requests (only used when transport is 'http').

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HTTP_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Host address to bind the HTTP server to (only used when transport is 'http').

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HTTP_PORT
requiredEnv.description: Port number for the HTTP server (only used when transport is 'http'). Use 0 for a random port.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_HTTP_RESPONSE_TYPE
requiredEnv.description: The HTTP response type for tool responses: 'sse' for Server-Sent Events, 'json' for standard JSON responses.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS
requiredEnv.description: Idle timeout for a client to disconnect (only applies to http transport).

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_INDEX_CHECK
requiredEnv.description: When set to true, enforces that query operations must use an index, rejecting queries that perform a collection scan.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_LOG_PATH
requiredEnv.description: Folder to store logs.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_LOGGERS
requiredEnv.description: Comma separated values of logger types.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MAX_ACTIVE_CONNECTIONS
requiredEnv.description: Maximum number of MongoDB connections a single scope (an MCP session by default, see connectionScope) can hold open. When exceeded, the scope's least-recently-used connection is closed and its connectionId revoked. The preconfigured connection does not count towards the limit.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MAX_BYTES_PER_QUERY
requiredEnv.description: The maximum size in bytes for results from a find or aggregate tool call. This serves as an upper bound for the responseBytesLimit parameter in those tools.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MAX_DOCUMENTS_PER_QUERY
requiredEnv.description: The maximum number of documents that can be returned by a find or aggregate tool call. For the find tool, the effective limit will be the smaller of this value and the tool's limit parameter.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MAX_SESSIONS
requiredEnv.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions the HTTP transport will hold in memory (only used when transport is 'http'). Each session holds a full server instance, transport, and timers, so choose a value based on your deployment's available memory; the default is a conservative safety net rather than a recommended production value.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MAX_TIME_M_S
requiredEnv.description: The maximum time in milliseconds that operations are allowed to run on the MongoDB server. When set, this value is passed as the maxTimeMS option to read operations such as find, aggregate, and count.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MCP_CLIENT_LOG_LEVEL
requiredEnv.description: Minimum severity level for log messages forwarded to the MCP client.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MONITORING_SERVER_FEATURES
requiredEnv.description: Features to expose on the monitoring server (only used when transport is 'http' and monitoringServerHost/monitoringServerPort are set).

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MONITORING_SERVER_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Host address to bind the monitoring HTTP server to (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `monitoringServerPort` must also be set.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_MONITORING_SERVER_PORT
requiredEnv.description: Port number for the monitoring HTTP server (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `monitoringServerHost` must also be set.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_NOTIFICATION_TIMEOUT_MS
requiredEnv.description: Notification timeout for a client to be aware of disconnect (only applies to http transport).

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_PREVIEW_FEATURES
requiredEnv.description: Comma separated values of preview features that are enabled.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY
requiredEnv.description: When set to true, only allows read, connect, and metadata operation types, disabling create/update/delete operations.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_TELEMETRY
requiredEnv.description: When set to disabled, disables telemetry collection.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_TRANSPORT
requiredEnv.description: Either 'stdio' or 'http'.

requiredEnv.name: MDB_MCP_VOYAGE_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: API key for Voyage AI embeddings service (required for creating Atlas Local deployments with auto-embed vector search capabilities).

requiredEnv.description: Transport for the MCP server: 'stdio' (default) or 'http' (the optional Streamable-HTTP transport).

requiredEnv.description: Bind host for the Streamable-HTTP transport (default 127.0.0.1).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_PORT
requiredEnv.description: Bind port for the Streamable-HTTP transport (1-65535; default 8000).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_PATH
requiredEnv.description: URL path the Streamable-HTTP transport serves on (default /mcp).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated allowlist of exact host:port values accepted by the Streamable-HTTP DNS-rebinding protection; empty defaults to loopback.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated allowlist of exact Origin values accepted by the Streamable-HTTP DNS-rebinding protection; empty defaults to loopback.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_TLS_AT_EDGE
requiredEnv.description: Set to 1 to acknowledge TLS is terminated at the edge; required to bind the Streamable-HTTP transport to a non-loopback host.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP
requiredEnv.description: Set to 1 to acknowledge running the Streamable-HTTP transport without a token verifier; required to boot the HTTP transport while auth is off.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ENABLED
requiredEnv.description: Set to 1 to enable MCP authentication (the composite token verifier + Resource-Server wiring); off by default.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated, ordered list of token-verifier strategies to compose (closed set: static, jwt, introspection, proxy, custom).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL
requiredEnv.description: OAuth authorization-server issuer URL advertised in the Protected-Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) when auth is enabled.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL
requiredEnv.description: The single resource identifier (RFC 8707 audience) for this server; the composite verifier re-checks every accepted token against it.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_REQUIRED_SCOPES
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated scopes a caller must hold; the SDK returns 403 insufficient_scope when a principal lacks one.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STATIC_TOKENS_FILE
requiredEnv.description: Path to the JSON secrets file for the static-bearer verifier (stores only SHA-256 digests of the accepted tokens).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_JWKS_URI
requiredEnv.description: HTTPS JWKS endpoint the `jwt` verifier fetches signing keys from (an OIDC provider's .well-known/jwks.json).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_ISSUER
requiredEnv.description: Expected `iss` claim for the `jwt` verifier; falls back to REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL when unset.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_ALGORITHMS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated PINNED, asymmetric-only JWS algorithms for the `jwt` verifier (default RS256,ES256); a symmetric algorithm on a JWKS source is refused.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_LEEWAY
requiredEnv.description: Clock-skew leeway in seconds applied to exp/nbf validation by the `jwt` verifier (default 60).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_JWKS_REFETCH_COOLDOWN
requiredEnv.description: Minimum seconds between JWKS refetches triggered by an unknown key id (the concurrency-safe flood guard; default 30).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_JWKS_TIMEOUT
requiredEnv.description: HTTP timeout in seconds for the `jwt` verifier's JWKS fetch (default 10).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_EXPECTED_TYP
requiredEnv.description: When set, the `jwt` verifier requires the JWT header `typ` to equal this (e.g. at+JWT per RFC 9068); unset skips the check.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_JWT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_JWKS_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Set to 1 to permit a private/link-local/loopback JWKS host (SSRF guard is on by default); off by default.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_ENDPOINT
requiredEnv.description: The `introspection` verifier's RFC 7662 endpoint URL (must be https://); the opaque token is POSTed here on every request (no caching).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_ID
requiredEnv.description: The client id the `introspection` verifier presents to the Authorization Server via HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_SECRET_ENV
requiredEnv.description: The NAME of the env var holding the introspection client secret (never the secret itself); must be present + non-empty at startup or the server refuses to start (fail-closed).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Set to 1 to permit a private/link-local/loopback introspection endpoint host (SSRF guard is on by default); off by default.

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_ALLOW_MISSING_AUD
requiredEnv.description: Set to 1 to accept an active introspection response that OMITS `aud` (many AS do); off by default (fail-closed reject).

requiredEnv.name: REBAR_MCP_AUTH_PROXY_SECRET_ENV
requiredEnv.description: The NAME of the env var holding the trusted-proxy shared secret (never the secret itself); must be present + non-empty at startup or the `proxy` verifier refuses to start (fail-closed).

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Hostname of the SMTP server, e.g. smtp.example.net.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_PORT
requiredEnv.description: Port. Defaults to 587 for starttls, 465 for implicit, 25 for none.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_TLS
requiredEnv.description: starttls (default), implicit or none. STARTTLS is required, never opportunistic.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_USER
requiredEnv.description: Username for SMTP authentication.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_PASSWORD
requiredEnv.description: Password or app-specific password for SMTP authentication.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_FROM
requiredEnv.description: The only sender this server will use, e.g. "Name <person@example.net>". There is no from parameter.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_REPLY_TO
requiredEnv.description: Reply-To header on every message, e.g. "Team <team@example.net>". Unset means no Reply-To header and replies go to SMTP_FROM. There is no reply_to parameter.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_ALLOW_SEND
requiredEnv.description: Set to "true" to register the sending tools. Defaults to false: the server cannot send until it is set.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated addresses and @domains this server may write to. Required with SMTP_ALLOW_SEND=true; "*" allows any.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_MAX_RECIPIENTS
requiredEnv.description: Maximum distinct recipients across To, Cc and Bcc in one message. Default 10.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_MAX_SENDS_PER_HOUR
requiredEnv.description: Sliding hourly cap on messages sent. Default 20.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES
requiredEnv.description: Maximum size of the composed message. Default 10485760.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES
requiredEnv.description: Maximum size of a single attachment. Default 5242880.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_ATTACHMENT_DIR
requiredEnv.description: Directory attachments are read from. Unset means attachments are unavailable.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_ATTACHMENT_TYPES
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated content types that may be attached. Defaults to a document and image allowlist.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_SIGNATURE
requiredEnv.description: Text appended below the standard signature delimiter of every message.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_AUDIT_LOG
requiredEnv.description: File the audit lines are appended to, in addition to stderr.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_ALLOW_TOOLS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated tool names, a prefix with one trailing *, or "essential" for the curated preset.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_DENY_TOOLS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated tool names or prefixes to remove, applied after SMTP_ALLOW_TOOLS.

requiredEnv.name: SMTP_INSECURE_TLS
requiredEnv.description: Set to "true" to accept self-signed certificates. Prefer a proper internal CA.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_PRIVATE_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Your wallet's private key/seed for the chosen chain. Optional: omit it to run read-only (discover/quote/register/budget/guide); set it to let the agent pay. Stays on your machine; the spend policy caps every payment.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_CHAIN
requiredEnv.description: Chain to pay on (default: base).

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_CHAINS
requiredEnv.description: Pay across several chains (instead of PIPRAIL_CHAIN): a comma-separated list, e.g. base,polygon,solana. Give each its own PIPRAIL_<CHAIN>_KEY (+ optional PIPRAIL_<CHAIN>_RPC_URL). The agent pays whichever chain a 402 asks for — the first listed that can settle — under one shared budget.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_MAX_AMOUNT
requiredEnv.description: Max spend per single payment, in token units (default: 0.10).

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_MAX_TOTAL
requiredEnv.description: Lifetime spend cap per token, in token units (default: 10.00).

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_MAX_TOTAL_DENOM
requiredEnv.description: Cross-token GRAND TOTAL: one spend cap per denomination across every stablecoin and chain, e.g. USD:20.00,EUR:5.00. Not a price oracle — sums tokens of the same unit, each counted 1:1. Native coins are excluded.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_MAX_PAYMENTS
requiredEnv.description: Lifetime cap on the NUMBER of payments, across every chain + token (e.g. 100).

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_MAX_PAYMENTS_PER_WINDOW
requiredEnv.description: Cap on the number of payments within PIPRAIL_WINDOW_SECONDS (a rolling rate limit; set PIPRAIL_WINDOW_SECONDS too).

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_WARN_AT_FRACTION
requiredEnv.description: Emit an early-warning event when spend crosses this fraction of any cap, e.g. 0.8 (80%). Needs PIPRAIL_EVENT_LOG to be visible.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_SPEND_LOG
requiredEnv.description: Path to a local append-only spend log. When set, the budget (lifetime, grand total, counts) SURVIVES a restart — hydrated from this file. No backend; you own the file.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_EVENT_LOG
requiredEnv.description: Mirror payment events (settled / declined / budget-threshold) as one-line JSON to 'stderr' or a file path — the operator's notification stream. Default: off.

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_TOKENS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated allowed token symbols, plus the alias 'native' for the chain's coin (default: USDC).

requiredEnv.name: PIPRAIL_SCHEMES
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated payment schemes to settle (default: onchain-proof). Add 'exact' (onchain-proof,exact) to also pay standard x402 servers GASLESS on EVM + Solana (method auto-selected). Add 'upto' to also pay metered x402 servers on EVM (Permit2): sign a MAX, the server settles the actual <= max.

requiredEnv.description: Log level for FastMCP internals and app loggers (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL). The -v CLI flag overrides to DEBUG.

requiredEnv.name: FASTMCP_ENABLE_RICH_LOGGING
requiredEnv.description: Set false for plain or structured JSON log output.

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_A1111_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Deprecated alias for IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_SD_WEBUI_HOST; logs a warning when used.

requiredEnv.description: Deprecated alias for IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_SD_WEBUI_MODEL; logs a warning when used.

requiredEnv.description: Directory where generated images are saved. Created automatically on first use.

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_GOOGLE_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Google API key. Enables the Gemini provider (gemini-3.1-flash-image and others) when set. Get a key at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey.

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_SD_WEBUI_HOST
requiredEnv.description: SD WebUI base URL (such as http://localhost:7860). Enables the SD WebUI provider when set. Compatible with AUTOMATIC1111, Forge, reForge, and Forge-neo.

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_SD_WEBUI_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: SD WebUI checkpoint name, used for model-aware preset detection (SD 1.5 / SDXL / Lightning) and checkpoint override. Unset uses the instance's current model.

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_DEFAULT_PROVIDER

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_STYLES_DIR
requiredEnv.description: Directory for style preset files (Markdown with YAML front matter). Created automatically if it does not exist.

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_ALLOW_LOCAL_FILE_INPUT

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_MAX_INPUT_IMAGE_BYTES

requiredEnv.name: IMAGE_GENERATION_MCP_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_KV_STORE_URL
requiredEnv.description: Persistent-state backend URL shared by every pvl-core subsystem that needs state. `memory://` is in-process and lost on restart; `file:///path` persists on one server; `redis://`, `dynamodb://` and `mongodb://` each need their matching extra. When unset, defaults to `file:///data/state` (the volume family Docker images mount), or to `memory://` (with a warning) on a host where that directory is not usable.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TOOLS_ALLOW
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated explicit tool names this instance exposes; every other tool is hidden from listings and cannot be invoked. Names matching no registered tool are inert. Mutually exclusive with `tools_deny`. Takes effect through `apply_tool_visibility`.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TOOLS_DENY
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated explicit tool names hidden from this instance (absent from listings, cannot be invoked). Names matching no registered tool are inert. Mutually exclusive with `tools_allow`. Takes effect through `apply_tool_visibility`.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SERVER_NAME
requiredEnv.description: Rename this server instance; defaults to the project name.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION
requiredEnv.description: Concise routing context that distinguishes this deployment's material or responsibility.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA
requiredEnv.description: Deployment-specific behavioral policy added to the generated MCP instructions.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS
requiredEnv.description: Legacy: replaces all generated MCP instructions (deprecated; use _INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION for routing and _INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA for policy).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_LEVEL
requiredEnv.description: Log level for every logger in the process, FastMCP's included (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL). The -v CLI flag overrides to DEBUG. The unprefixed FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL still works for one major version and logs a deprecation warning.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_FORMAT
requiredEnv.description: Log rendering. rich is one colour event key=value line per record, for a terminal; json is one JSON object per record, for a collector. Unset picks rich when stderr is a terminal and json everywhere else, so a container or journald gets JSON with no configuration.

requiredEnv.name: OLLAMA_HOST
requiredEnv.description: Ollama server URL for the ollama embedding provider. Bare (not MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_-prefixed), matching the Ollama ecosystem convention.

requiredEnv.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: OpenAI API key for the openai embedding provider, and the fallback key for the summarize tool when MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_API_KEY is unset. Bare (not MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_-prefixed), matching the OpenAI ecosystem convention.

requiredEnv.name: VOYAGE_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Voyage AI API key for the voyage embedding provider. Bare (not MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_-prefixed), matching the OPENAI_API_KEY / OLLAMA_HOST convention. Setting it never auto-selects the provider; choose it explicitly with MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=voyage.

requiredEnv.name: OPENAI_BASE_URL
requiredEnv.description: Bare fallback for MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_BASE_URL (embeddings). For the summarize tool it only routes traffic when an API key already enables the feature; it never enables summarize by itself.

requiredEnv.name: OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: Bare fallback for MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S
requiredEnv.description: Maximum seconds an index-backed tool or resource waits for the FTS index to become queryable during a cold-start background build before raising IndexUnavailableError(reason="timeout"). Increase for large vaults.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S
requiredEnv.description: Maximum seconds an index-querying read tool waits for the IndexWriter to drain when called with wait_for_pending_writes=true. On timeout the tool answers from the current index and reports index_stale=true in the response _meta.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR
requiredEnv.description: Path to the markdown vault directory. When it does not exist, or the server cannot access it, the server starts but every tool fails with a message saying which until it is fixed (managed git mode clones into it). Symbolic links inside the vault are followed on Python 3.13+.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_READ_ONLY
requiredEnv.description: Set to true to hide the write tools (write, edit, append, delete, rename, move_folder, fetch, git_sync, the okf_* tools, create_upload_link) and serve a search-only vault.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_WRITE_PROTECT_EXISTING
requiredEnv.description: Refuse a write that would overwrite an existing file when no if_match etag is supplied. Deliberate replacement still works: read the file first, then pass if_match. Unaffected: edit, append, delete, rename. Set to false to allow blind overwrites.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DISABLE_APPS_UI
requiredEnv.description: Hide the MCP Apps UI tools (browse_vault, show_context) from the tool listing for clients that do not render MCP Apps panels.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INDEX_PATH
requiredEnv.description: Path to the SQLite FTS5 index file; unset keeps the index in memory. Set it for persistence across restarts.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_STATE_PATH
requiredEnv.description: Path to the change-tracking state file. Defaults to {SOURCE_DIR}/.markdown_vault_mcp/state.json.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDINGS_PATH
requiredEnv.description: Path to the numpy embeddings file; required to enable semantic search.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INDEXED_FIELDS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields promoted to the tag index for structured filtering. Changing it cold-rebuilds the index once on next startup; SEARCHABLE_FIELDS inherits this value when unset.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_REQUIRED_FIELDS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields required on every document; documents missing any are excluded from the index.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EXCLUDE
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated glob patterns excluded from scanning, e.g. .obsidian/**,.trash/**.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TITLE_FIELD
requiredEnv.description: Frontmatter field used as the document title (falls back to title, the first H1, then the filename). Changing it cold-rebuilds the index once on next startup.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SEARCHABLE_FIELDS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields whose text values become keyword-searchable and enrich first-chunk embeddings. Inherits INDEXED_FIELDS when unset; the sentinel none means filterable but not searchable. Changing it cold-rebuilds the index and re-embeds once on next startup.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TEMPLATES_FOLDER
requiredEnv.description: Relative folder where note templates live (used by the create_from_template prompt).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_PROMPTS_FOLDER
requiredEnv.description: Directory of .md prompt files that extend or override built-in prompts; a relative path is resolved against SOURCE_DIR.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CONVENTIONS_FILE
requiredEnv.description: Filename of the per-folder conventions files surfaced to clients at write time (bare .md filename without glob characters). Set to none to disable folder conventions.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_MODE
requiredEnv.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) read semantics. With auto (the default), read annotations switch on when the vault declares an OKF version in its root index.md. Use off to disable OKF semantics entirely, or on to force them for an undeclared vault. Annotations are read-only; write behavior is never affected.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_WRITE
requiredEnv.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) enforced write layer. When true on an OKF-active vault, the server stamps generated provenance on each write and clears any verified attestation when a note's content changes. It also keeps each written folder's log.md and index.md current, and exposes the okf_verify tool. Requires OKF_MODE to be auto or on (a true value with OKF_MODE=off is a config error). Off by default.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_VERIFY
requiredEnv.description: How the okf_verify tool attributes a human review. This applies only when OKF_WRITE is on, which gates the tool. With elicit (the default), okf_verify asks the human to confirm the review through an MCP elicitation, then records the attestation only on an affirmative reply. It fails closed when the client cannot elicit or the human declines, so a model holding the human's token cannot self-attest. Set trust-auth instead to attribute to a token's sub claim with no confirmation; it rejects static bearer credentials and other client-ID-only identities. This is safe only when the sole caller is a human-driven UI. Set off to hide the tool, leaving attestation to external tooling. A non-default value with OKF_WRITE off is a config error.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_ATTACHMENT_EXTENSIONS
requiredEnv.description: Comma-separated allowed attachment extensions (e.g. pdf,png,jpg); case and a leading dot are ignored, so PDF and .pdf name the same type. Use * to allow every non-markdown file. Unset selects the built-in allowlist. A link whose target has a listed extension is not part of the link graph; changing the list rebuilds the index once.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB
requiredEnv.description: Maximum attachment size in MB returned by read / accepted by write; 0 disables the limit.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_NOTE_READ_BYTES
requiredEnv.description: Maximum bytes returned by a full-document read of a note; use `read(path, section=…)` for partial reads. 0 disables the limit.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DEFAULT_SEARCH_MODE
requiredEnv.description: Mode used when a search call omits 'mode': auto, keyword, semantic, or hybrid. The default 'auto' picks hybrid when embeddings are configured and keyword when they are not. Pin 'keyword' to keep unqualified searches off the embedding provider (each hybrid or semantic search embeds the query, which costs an API call on a metered provider). A configured semantic/hybrid default also degrades to keyword without embeddings, so no setting can make a vault unsearchable; an explicit mode= argument is never downgraded.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CHUNKS_PER_FILE
requiredEnv.description: Maximum chunks returned per document in search results.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SNIPPET_WORDS
requiredEnv.description: Width of the snippet window (words) in search results; 0 returns full chunk content.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LENGTH_DOWNWEIGHT_ALPHA
requiredEnv.description: Down-weights longer chunks in ranking: score / (1 + alpha * log(chunk_count)).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_CHUNK_WORDS
requiredEnv.description: Word cap per chunk; the adaptive chunker splits at deeper heading levels, then paragraph/word boundaries, to respect it. Match it to the embedding model's context. A reindex applies a new value.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS
requiredEnv.description: Character cap enforced alongside MAX_CHUNK_WORDS to bound token-dense chunks. Unset derives min(1500, model context * 2.8). Set a positive value for an exact cap, or -1 to scale with the model's full context (can exhaust memory on long-context models). A reindex applies a new value.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CHUNK_OVERLAP_WORDS
requiredEnv.description: Words of overlap between adjacent budget-split fragments of the same heading section (0 disables). A reindex applies a new value.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FOLDER_WEIGHTS
requiredEnv.description: Folder-prefix score multipliers (`prefix:weight` pairs, comma-separated, weights > 0) applied to all search modes; the deepest matching prefix wins (sessions:0.5 demotes sessions/**).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FTS_WEIGHTS
requiredEnv.description: Per-column BM25 weights (`column:weight` pairs, comma-separated, weights >= 0) for keyword ranking. Columns: path, title, folder, heading, content, summary.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER
requiredEnv.description: Embedding provider: openai, voyage, ollama, or fastembed. Unset auto-detects from the environment (never voyage). Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works with openai plus OPENAI_BASE_URL; see the embeddings guide.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OLLAMA_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: Ollama embedding model name.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OLLAMA_CPU_ONLY
requiredEnv.description: Force Ollama to embed on CPU only.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: Voyage AI embedding model name.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_BASE_URL
requiredEnv.description: OpenAI-compatible API base URL for embeddings; the bare OPENAI_BASE_URL is honoured as a fallback.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: OpenAI-compatible embedding model name; the bare OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL is honoured as a fallback.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FASTEMBED_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: FastEmbed model name.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR
requiredEnv.description: FastEmbed model cache directory (in Docker, stored under /data/state/fastembed).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBED_CONTEXT
requiredEnv.description: Enrich embedding input with the note title, chunk heading, and (first chunk) searchable-field values. Flipping it re-embeds the whole vault once on next startup.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S
requiredEnv.description: Per-request wall-clock budget in seconds for a single embedding HTTP call (OpenAI/Ollama). The local FastEmbed backend runs in-process with no network call and ignores this. CPU-only or large-model workloads may need 60-120 s; raise this if batches time out.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE
requiredEnv.description: Number of chunks sent per embedding request. Smaller batches shorten each request (useful under a tight timeout on slow models) at the cost of more round-trips.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_TOKEN
requiredEnv.description: Token/password for HTTPS git auth; remotes must be HTTPS when set.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_REPO_URL
requiredEnv.description: HTTPS remote URL for managed git mode: the server clones into an empty SOURCE_DIR on startup (or validates an existing origin) and enables the pull loop, auto-commit, and deferred push.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_USERNAME
requiredEnv.description: Username for HTTPS git auth prompts (x-access-token for GitHub, oauth2 for GitLab, the account name for Bitbucket).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_PULL_INTERVAL_S
requiredEnv.description: Seconds between git fetch + fast-forward update attempts; 0 disables periodic pull.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_PUSH_DELAY_S
requiredEnv.description: Seconds of write-idle time before pushing; 0 pushes only on shutdown.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_NAME
requiredEnv.description: Git committer name for auto-commits; set this in Docker where git config user.name is empty.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL
requiredEnv.description: Git committer email for auto-commits.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_NAME_CLAIM
requiredEnv.description: OIDC claim key used as the commit author name (e.g. name); overrides GIT_COMMIT_NAME per request when an OIDC token is present. The claim is resolved when the tool call arrives and carried to the background commit, so it applies on every write. A configured claim the token does not carry is reported once at WARNING and the static identity is used.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL_CLAIM
requiredEnv.description: OIDC claim key used as the commit author email (e.g. email); overrides GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL per request when an OIDC token is present. Resolved and carried the same way as the name claim.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_LFS
requiredEnv.description: Run git lfs pull on startup to fetch LFS-tracked attachments; set to false for repos without LFS.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER
requiredEnv.description: Watch the vault for external filesystem changes; auto-disabled when git pull is active or a webhook can deliver (HTTP/SSE transports only). Requires the file-watcher extra.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER_DEBOUNCE_S
requiredEnv.description: Seconds of quiet after the last filesystem event before reindexing.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER_ROOT_FLOOR
requiredEnv.description: Keep the non-recursive watch on the vault root; set false to register zero source-dir-rooted FSEvents streams (avoids repeated macOS access prompts on a home-rooted vault) at the cost of root-level files relying on scans.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BOOT_REINDEX
requiredEnv.description: Reconcile offline changes at startup by reindexing once the initial build completes. Set false on a large vault to start without paying a full filesystem scan per server start; changes made while no server was running are then invisible until a reindex runs (the reindex tool, or 'markdown-vault-mcp reindex'). Note that `index_stale` reports writer idleness, not agreement with disk, so it reads false while the index may still differ from the vault.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
requiredEnv.description: Shared secret for the GitHub push-event webhook; when set, mounts POST /github-webhook on HTTP/SSE transports to trigger an immediate pull + reindex on push events.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_TOKEN
requiredEnv.description: Signing token for the GitLab push-event webhook (GitLab 19.0+); when set, mounts POST /gitlab-webhook on HTTP/SSE transports to trigger an immediate pull + reindex on push events. GitLab generates this value; copy the `whsec_` token it shows under Generate signing token rather than inventing one. Deliveries are authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 over the webhook id, timestamp and body, and a delivery older than 5 minutes is rejected.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN
requiredEnv.description: Secret token for the GitLab push-event webhook, GitLab's plain-text form and the only one below 19.0; also mounts POST /gitlab-webhook. It proves nothing about the body and cannot expire, so prefer the signing token where the GitLab version offers it. Setting both accepts either, which is how an existing webhook migrates.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_PROVIDER
requiredEnv.description: Summarization backend (only openai is recognised). Unset auto-detects: the backend activates when credentials or an explicit endpoint are present.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: API key for the OpenAI-compatible summarize endpoint; the bare OPENAI_API_KEY is honoured as a fallback. Unset works for keyless local endpoints (Ollama).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_BASE_URL
requiredEnv.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint base URL for the summarize tool; setting it enables the tool even without an API key. The bare OPENAI_BASE_URL routes traffic only when a key already enables the feature.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_MODEL
requiredEnv.description: Chat model id used for summaries.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_MAX_TOKENS
requiredEnv.description: Upper bound on generated tokens per summarize call; on reasoning models this budget also covers internal reasoning tokens.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_MAX_NOTES
requiredEnv.description: Cap on the number of notes summarised in one call (subtree expansion truncates to this many).

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_MAX_INPUT_CHARS
requiredEnv.description: Aggregate cap on note characters sent to the model in one call; excess is truncated with a flag on the result.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT
requiredEnv.description: Per-request wall-clock budget in seconds for a single summarize backend call; keep it below the MCP client's request timeout so the server-side error wins the race.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_TTL_DEFAULT_S
requiredEnv.description: Link lifetime in seconds when the caller requests no explicit TTL.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_TTL_MAX_S
requiredEnv.description: Ceiling in seconds a caller-requested link TTL is clamped to.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_GRACE_TTL_S
requiredEnv.description: Post-success grace window in seconds: a served token's TTL shrinks to this so a stalled transfer can retry within it.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_LEASE_S
requiredEnv.description: Crashed-handler reclaim window in seconds for an in-flight reservation.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES
requiredEnv.description: Maximum size in bytes of a single upload.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_JOBS_SOFT_DEADLINE_S
requiredEnv.description: Seconds a long-running tool call may run in the foreground before it is promoted to a background job and a job handle is returned instead.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_JOBS_RESULT_TTL_S
requiredEnv.description: Seconds a background-job record (working or finished) is retained for polling before it expires from the store.

requiredEnv.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_JOBS_MAX_PER_SUBJECT
requiredEnv.description: Maximum live background jobs per calling subject; further promotions are rejected until older records expire.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_TRIAL_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Recommended path: skip this UI and run `q402_doctor` after install - it stores secrets in ~/.q402/mcp.env, which the server auto-loads. Fill this field directly ONLY if your MCP client manages secrets for you. Value is a Free Trial API key from https://q402.quackai.ai/event - BNB Chain (permanent) + Base (permanent) + Mantle limited-time (2026-08-21~08-28 UTC+9), 500 sponsored TXs, gas covered by Q402. Avalanche trial has ended. BNB and Base payments auto-route to this key when set (same rule for q402_pay and q402_batch_pay up to 5 recipients).

requiredEnv.name: Q402_MULTICHAIN_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Recommended path: skip this UI and run `q402_doctor` after install - it stores secrets in ~/.q402/mcp.env, which the server auto-loads. Fill this field directly ONLY if your MCP client manages secrets for you. Value is a Paid Multichain API key from https://q402.quackai.ai/payment - full 12-chain support with per-chain Gas Tank. Auto-routed for non-BNB payments and whenever keyScope='multichain' is chosen.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_PRIVATE_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Mode A - real EOA signing. Hex-encoded EVM private key (0x + 64 hex chars) of YOUR MetaMask wallet, used to sign payment authorizations LOCALLY on your machine. After your first payment that wallet shows as 'Smart account' in MetaMask (EIP-7702 delegation, reversible via q402_clear_delegation). Use a fresh wallet, not your main one. Skip this and pick Mode B (Q402_AGENTIC_PRIVATE_KEY) or Mode C (server-managed Agent Wallet) if you'd rather keep your MetaMask untouched. Recommended path: run q402_doctor after install - it stores secrets in ~/.q402/mcp.env, which the server auto-loads.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_AGENTIC_PRIVATE_KEY
requiredEnv.description: Mode B - local Agent Wallet signing. Hex-encoded EVM private key (0x + 64 hex chars) exported from your Agent Wallet at https://q402.quackai.ai/dashboard -> Agent tab -> Export. Signs LOCALLY just like Mode A, but the signer is your dedicated Agent Wallet - your MetaMask EOA is never touched. Pick this for AI-agent automation when you want a dedicated purse with per-tx + daily caps you set on the dashboard.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_ENABLE_REAL_PAYMENTS
requiredEnv.description: Live-mode switch. 0 = sandbox (test mode, no funds move - every q402_pay returns a fake hash). 1 = real on-chain payments. Default 1 since v0.5.11: safe because mode only flips to live when a live API key (q402_live_*) is set AND one of (a) a valid 32-byte private key for local signing modes, OR (b) walletMode="agentic-server" with Q402_MULTICHAIN_API_KEY for the server-managed Agent Wallet path. Without either combination, the server stays in sandbox regardless of this flag.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_MAX_AMOUNT_PER_CALL
requiredEnv.description: Per-call USD-equivalent cap for USDC/USDT/RLUSD. Any such q402_pay request with amount above this is rejected before signing. Q (QuackAI) is exempt by design (your own token; recipient allowlist + confirmation still apply). Lower this for a tighter agent blast-radius; raise for treasury-grade transfers.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS
requiredEnv.description: Optional comma-separated lowercase EVM addresses. When set, q402_pay rejects any recipient not on this allowlist.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_RELAY_BASE_URL
requiredEnv.description: Override for the Q402 relay endpoint. Defaults to https://q402.quackai.ai/api. Set explicitly when running against a self-hosted Q402 deployment or a non-canonical environment.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_AGENT_WALLET_ADDRESS
requiredEnv.description: Server-managed Agent Wallet picker (walletMode='agentic-server' only). Lowercased agent wallet address (the hex 0x... shown on the Agent tab of your dashboard) selecting which of your Agent Wallets to spend from when you hold more than one (max 10 per owner). Omit to use the default wallet. Ignored for the local-signing modes that carry their own private key.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_API_KEY
requiredEnv.description: DEPRECATED legacy single-key env from pre-v0.5.0 installs. The server still reads it as a silent fallback so existing setups keep working, but new users should pick a scoped variant instead. Q402_TRIAL_API_KEY (Free Trial, BNB Chain + Base) and Q402_MULTICHAIN_API_KEY (full 12-chain surface) are designed to coexist - BNB and Base payments auto-route to the trial key, other chains use multichain. Only set Q402_API_KEY if you are migrating an existing pre-v0.5.0 install; do NOT set it alongside the scoped variants on a fresh install.

requiredEnv.name: Q402_WALLET_ID
requiredEnv.description: DEPRECATED soft-migration alias for Q402_AGENT_WALLET_ADDRESS (one release of overlap from v0.6.0). The server still accepts it but logs a deprecation notice. New installs should set Q402_AGENT_WALLET_ADDRESS directly.

When set, every q402_x402_fetch payment includes your code as the client/intermediary in the x402 payment extension so payments are attributed onchain. Format: 1-32 lowercase letters, numbers, or underscores. Leave unset to disable attribution.
